subject: Discovery recap and next steps — latency, streaming UX, and concurrency targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Discovery recap and next steps — latency, streaming UX, and concurrency targets

Hi Simon — thanks again for a productive first call. Quick recap while everything is fresh and to confirm next steps on our side.

Key pain points you called out
- End-user streaming experience feels laggy: token-by-token updates arrive irregularly and sometimes stall mid-response.
- Search/assist p95 tail is higher than acceptable for fast flows (you reported ~800–1,200 ms on peak).
- Heavy spikes during promotions cause timeouts / apparent rate-limit errors for embedded assistants.

Current stack summary (from your notes)
- Models: fine-tuned LLaMA derivative serving via SageMaker multi-model endpoints.
- Frontend: Websocket-based streaming (in-house wrapper over socket.io).
- Infra: single-region AWS (us-west-2), auto-scaling but with cold-starts on GPU-backed instances.

Success criteria you gave
- p95 (inference) target: <= 250 ms for 0–512 token completions under normal load.
- Streaming token RTT target: < 80 ms end-to-end (server → client).
- Sustained QPS: 600 req/s, burst up to ~2,400 req/s during peak promotions.
- Graceful degradation: fall back to smaller model with < 40% quality loss under capacity pressure.

What Redwood can do next (proposed)
1) Run a targeted latency bench on a representative prompt set (we'll need your sample prompts & tokenization expectations). I attached a short latency/template we use to capture the metrics we’ll measure.
2) Tech deep-dive (60 min) with Karthik to walk through your streaming stack, TLS termination, and caching opportunities.
3) Proposed quick wins: prefix caching for repeated prompts, adjust batching windows, and a streaming buffer tweak to reduce jitter.
4) If results look promising, we can propose a Dedicated capacity estimate and a pilot SLO for a 4‑week evaluation.

Immediate asks from you
- Share a 48–72 hour production telemetry dump (sample traces/aggregates) and 10–20 representative prompts (anonymized).
- Confirm 2 windows that work for a 60‑min tech deep-dive next week.

Attachments: redwood_latency_template.xlsx — this is our short CSV/XLS template with fields we use to define prompt sets and success thresholds.

If any part of the recap is off, tell me and I’ll correct — otherwise aim to get the telemetry + prompts by Tue 02/24 so we can run an initial bench and come back with numbers.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Discovery recap and next steps — latency, streaming UX, and concurrency targets

Thanks Marissa — this is great and accurately captures what we discussed. A few clarifications/notes:

- The 800–1,200 ms numbers are p95 from our edge logs during peak promo windows (we see p50 around 180–220 ms). The p95 jumps mostly correlate with larger responses ~600–800 tokens.
- Streaming library: we run a custom websocket layer on top of nginx + node. Token buffering currently happens client-side which is part of the jitter issue.
- Concurrency: 600 sustained is our safe baseline; spikes historically hit 2,100–2,500 active concurrent streams, sustained for ~8–12 minutes during promos.

We'll bundle a small sanitized telemetry pack and 15 prompts by Monday EOD. I attached a small sample of our metrics export (acme_system_metrics_week6.zip) — let me know if the format works for you.

One business question: can you outline what Dedicated looks like (rough ballpark monthly) for a pilot that supports the 2,400 burst target? We're evaluating cost vs. building more capacity ourselves.

Happy to meet next Tue afternoon or Wed morning for the tech deep-dive — 60 minutes is perfect.

Simon

Hi Simon — quick tech checklist and a few targeted asks so we can run the right benches.

Checklist (what we need to know)
- Model & tokenizer: which LLaMA fork + tokenizer (vocab size / BPE specifics)? Are you using a causal LM or mixed encoder-decoder flows?
- Typical prompt/response lengths: median/95th token lengths for prompts and completions.
- Batch tolerance: can your client tolerate small batching delays (e.g., 10–30 ms) in exchange for cost/throughput improvements?
- Streaming protocol: current websocket stack, heartbeat, and whether you can support server-sent events or direct SSE/Websocket without additional buffering.
- TLS termination point: do you terminate TLS at nginx or at the app layer on the instances?
- KV caching: do you use any prefix or query caching that could be offloaded to an inference cache layer?

Proposed benchmark we can run once we have artifacts
- 1) Single-request p95/avg for 0–512 tokens at low concurrency (10 parallel connections)
- 2) Sustained throughput ramp up to 600 RPS with 5-minute holds at each step (measure p95 + token RTT)
- 3) Burst test to 2,500 concurrent streams for 10 minutes (observe fallbacks, queueing, and tail latency)
- 4) Streaming token RTT measurement: token emission latency distribution (server send → client receive) with real prompt set

Schedule: I can run an initial bench Monday afternoon if you get us the telemetry & prompts early. For the tech deep-dive, I’m available Tue 02/24 at 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 02/25 at 09:00–10:00 PT.

One note on Dedicated sizing: there are several knobs (gpu type, instance count, batching windows, KV cache) — I’ll scope a rough pilot estimate after the bench and we can circle back to commercial.

-Karthik
